threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Tube' instead of just 'the train'—locals rarely bother with the full name.
Saw a guy on the 333 singing full operas. The driver just shook his head and smiled. You wouldn't get that on the day buses!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found a hidden garden behind the old brewery on Weserstraße, filled with locals barbecuing and laughing, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand open at 2 AM, serving up greasy goodness to late-night partiers right after the clubs close.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You'll notice the locals refuse to use the term 'Muni' when talking about the bus. They call it 'The 12' or just 'the bus'—it's all about familiarity.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a bus driver shake hands with a regular after helping them get their dog on board. Only in SF do you see that kind of connection in transit.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all shops close in the afternoon, but many in Gràcia reopen for late-night tapas runs. You just have to know where to look.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're recent when they order a café con leche and expect it to come in a to-go cup, totally baffled by the sit-down culture.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—that's a dead giveaway. Locals know the difference when it comes to getting around.
Caught the 35 last night; a guy in Crocs was karaoke-ing to his earbuds like he was on stage at the O2. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in full lederhosen at the corner shop, casually buying a pack of ciggies and some falafel. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find döner shops that double as art galleries, where the kebab tastes like a masterpiece and street art adorns the walls.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they react when BART's down—it's not just a delay, it's a sigh and a roll of the eyes like they've seen it all before.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a woman singing opera on the 47 bus yesterday. Whole bus was silent, even the usual loudmouths. Felt like we shared a secret moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just about the park and squares, but it’s the scent of fresh pa amb tomàquet wafting from corner bars that truly makes it special.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones pulling out Google Maps in the middle of Plaça Reial, oblivious to the street performers and the locals just hanging out.
